body:
## Pull request overview

This PR upgrades the `lookup` field UX to an enterprise-style, two-level record picking flow (typeahead popover + full-featured picker dialog) and extends the lookup metadata schema to support richer configuration.

**Changes:**
- Extended `LookupFieldMetadata` in `@object-ui/types` with column and filter configuration types (`LookupColumnDef`, `LookupFilterDef`) plus `lookup_columns`, `lookup_page_size`, `lookup_filters`, and `description_field`.
- Added `RecordPickerDialog` to `@object-ui/fields` with table rendering, server-side pagination, sorting, debounced search, and keyboard navigation; wired it into `LookupField` via “Show All Results”.
- Added documentation, changelog/roadmap entries, and a new test suite covering dialog behavior and LookupField integration.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 9 out of 9 changed files in this pull request and generated 12 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/types/src/index.ts | Re-exports new lookup-related types from `@object-ui/types`. |
| packages/types/src/field-types.ts | Adds `LookupColumnDef` / `LookupFilterDef` and extends `LookupFieldMetadata` for enterprise picker configuration. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/RecordPickerDialog.tsx | Introduces the new full-screen record picker dialog with table UX, pagination, sorting, search, and keyboard nav. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx | Converts Level 1 to a Popover typeahead and integrates Level 2 dialog via “Show All Results”. |
| packages/fields/src/record-picker.test.tsx | Adds tests for RecordPickerDialog and LookupField integration scenarios. |
| packages/fields/src/index.tsx | Exports `RecordPickerDialog` from the fields package. |
| content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx | Documents the new two-level picker UX and schema config (`lookup_columns`, `lookup_page_size`, etc.). |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks the enterprise record picker milestone as complete. |
| CHANGELOG.md | Adds an Unreleased “Added” entry describing the new picker capabilities and schema updates. |
</details>

Prop comment says `columns` “Defaults to [displayField, descriptionField]”, but there is no `descriptionField` prop and the fallback logic only infers a single column from `displayField`. Please update the prop documentation or implement the described default behavior.

Docs list **Base Filters** (`lookup_filters`) as a supported feature, but neither `LookupField` nor `RecordPickerDialog` currently applies `lookup_filters` to DataSource queries. Either wire `lookup_filters` into query construction (e.g., `QueryParams.$filter`) or remove/mark this as not yet implemented to avoid misleading users.

When the user is not on page 1, `handleSearchChange` sets `currentPage(1)` and also schedules a debounced `fetchRecords`. Because the fetch `useEffect` runs on `currentPage` changes, this can trigger an immediate fetch with the new query (defeating the debounce) and then a second fetch 300ms later. Consider restructuring so search changes don’t cause an extra immediate fetch (e.g., separate effect keyed on `currentPage/currentSort` using a debounced query value).

`lookup_filters` is introduced on `LookupFieldMetadata` and documented as “base filters applied to every Record Picker query”, but there is no corresponding implementation in `LookupField`/`RecordPickerDialog` to translate these into `QueryParams.$filter`. This makes the schema field misleading and prevents the intended restriction behavior.

The debounced search timer is not cleared when the dialog closes, so typing and immediately closing can still trigger `fetchRecords` after close. That can cause extra network requests and can repopulate `records` while `open=false`, leading to stale results flashing on the next open. Clear the debounce timer in the close/reset path and/or ignore late responses when the dialog is closed (e.g., request id / AbortController).

Sorting is triggered via `onClick` on `<TableHead>` (a `<th>`), which is not keyboard-accessible by default. For accessibility, the interactive control should be a focusable element (e.g., a `<button>` inside the header cell) and support Enter/Space activation, while keeping `aria-sort` on the `<th>`.

`lookup_filters` is added to the metadata types/docs, but `LookupField` does not read it or pass it to Level 2, and Level 1 queries don’t apply any base filter. To make `lookup_filters` effective, read it from `fieldMeta` and include it in the DataSource query (likely via `QueryParams.$filter`).

The “Show All Results (N)” logic depends on `totalCount`, but `fetchLookupData` doesn’t request totals (`QueryParams.$count`), and `QueryResult.total` is optional “if requested”. With many DataSource implementations this will keep `totalCount === displayedCount`, so the button never appears even when more results exist. Consider setting `$count: true` in the Level 1 query (and/or using `hasMore`) so the two-level interaction works reliably.

The debounce test uses real timers and `waitFor({ timeout: 500 })` to accommodate the 300ms delay. This can be flaky under load. Since the repo already uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` elsewhere, consider switching this test to fake timers and advancing time deterministically before asserting the debounced fetch.

Changelog claims `lookup_filters` are supported as “base filter configuration”, but the current implementation does not apply `lookup_filters` in either Level 1 queries or `RecordPickerDialog` queries. Please either implement filter application or adjust the changelog entry so it matches actual behavior.

`LookupColumnDef.type` docstring says the Record Picker “uses getCellRenderer for formatting” when `type` is provided, but `RecordPickerDialog` currently ignores this field and renders via `getCellValue` only. Either implement type-aware rendering in the dialog or adjust this comment to avoid promising behavior that doesn’t exist yet.

`QueryResult.total` is documented as “Total number of records (if requested)”. `RecordPickerDialog` relies on `result.total` for pagination, but never sets `params.$count = true`, so many DataSource implementations will return `total` as undefined and pagination will break (no way to navigate beyond page 1). Consider requesting `$count` (and/or honoring `result.hasMore`) when building query params.
